content: Mefenamic acid is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke compared to individuals who do not take NSAIDs. These cardiovascular events can occur without warning and may result in death. The risk is higher for those who use NSAIDs for extended periods. Inform your doctor if you or your family have a history of heart disease, heart attack, or stroke, if you smoke, or if you have high cholesterol, high blood pressure, or diabetes. Seek emergency medical attention immediately if you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side of the body, or slurred speech. Do not take mefenamic acid before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. NSAIDs, including mefenamic acid, can cause ulcers, bleeding, or perforations in the stomach or intestines, which may occur at any time during treatment, often without warning, and can be fatal. The risk is higher in older adults, those in poor health, or individuals who consume large amounts of alcohol while taking this medication. Inform your doctor if you are taking anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), aspirin, other NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), or oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, prednisone). Also, let your doctor know if you have a history of ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, or other bleeding disorders. Stop taking mefenamic acid and contact your doctor if you experience stomach pain, heartburn, vomiting blood or material resembling coffee grounds, blood in the stool, or black, tarry stools. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor will monitor your symptoms and may order tests to assess your response to the medication. Inform your doctor about how you are feeling to ensure the correct dosage is prescribed with minimal risk of serious side effects. You will receive a Medication Guide from your doctor or pharmacist when starting treatment and with each prescription refill. Read it carefully and ask any questions you may have. Mefenamic acid is prescribed to relieve mild to moderate pain, including menstrual pain. It belongs to the NSAID class of medications and works by inhibiting the production of substances in the body that cause pain, fever, and inflammation. Mefenamic acid is available as an oral capsule and is typically taken with food every six hours as needed for up to one week. Follow the prescription label instructions carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed and do not exceed the prescribed dose or frequency. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking mefenamic acid, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to mefenamic acid, aspirin, other NSAIDs, or any inactive ingredients in the capsules. Ask your pharmacist for a list of inactive ingredients. Provide your doctor with a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Mention any medications listed in the Important Warning section, as well as antacids, ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril, enalapril), diuretics, amiodarone, clopidogrel, fluconazole, lithium, methotrexate, and others. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, especially if accompanied by frequent nasal congestion or nasal polyps, swelling in the extremities, or liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, particularly in the last few months of pregnancy, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking mefenamic acid, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking mefenamic acid. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Mefenamic acid may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience diarrhea, constipation, gas, bloating, headache, dizziness, nervousness, or ringing in the ears, especially if these symptoms persist or worsen. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. Stop taking mefenamic acid and contact your doctor if you experience blurred vision, unexplained weight gain, fever, blisters, rash, itching, hives, swelling of the face or extremities, difficulty breathing or swallowing, pale skin, rapid heartbeat, unusual bleeding or bruising, fatigue, loss of appetite, upper right abdominal pain, flu-like symptoms, yellowing of the skin or eyes, discolored or bloody urine, back pain, or painful urination. Report serious side effects to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store mefenamic acid in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual collapses or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include extreme fatigue, stomach pain, vomiting (with or without blood), black or bloody stools, slowed breathing, or loss of consciousness. Before undergoing any laboratory tests, inform your doctor and laboratory personnel that you are taking mefenamic acid. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
